skill.name: executor-verification
skill.description: Verify software requirements with observed command output, commit-bound evidence, explicit gap statuses, and a human completion gate.
skill.summary: Turn completion claims into requirement-level evidence and report exactly what remains unproven.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: All 155 static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, intended local verification, companion paths, or protective secret-handling guidance. Two semantic workflow risks concern unisolated regression reverts and retained evidence after secret-scan failures. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or exfiltration; companion helper implementations are outside the two reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Regression verification requests code reverts without an isolation or preservation procedure.
remediation.suggestion: Run the red-green cycle in a disposable worktree with a recorded baseline, preserving user changes and restoring the tested state before capture.

remediation.issue: Secret-scan recovery can leave sensitive originals beside redacted evidence attempts.
remediation.suggestion: Quarantine failed captures before tracking or committing them, scan every retained attempt, and document secure removal plus credential rotation when exposure occurred.

semantic_findings.title: Regression Verification Reverts Fixes Without Isolation
semantic_findings.description: The regression workflow says "Revert the fix" and "Restore the fix" without an isolated worktree or recovery checkpoint. Following it in a shared worktree can discard edits or disrupt concurrent work.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The ordered steps explicitly require reverting and restoring code, but provide no isolation or preservation procedure. No destructive command is specified, so damage depends on implementation.

semantic_findings.title: Secret Recovery Does Not Address Retained Evidence Copies
semantic_findings.description: After a secret finding, the runner says "redact and rewrite" through the evidence helper. The storage policy creates new attempt files instead of overwriting, so sensitive originals may remain in tracked evidence.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Recovery requests another write while the documented helper preserves earlier attempts. No cleanup or quarantine of detected sensitive originals is specified; the helper implementation is outside this audit.

content.user_title: Verify Completion Claims With Recorded Evidence
content.value_statement: Completion claims can hide failed, skipped, or untested requirements. This skill guides requirement-level verification with observed output, commit-bound evidence, and explicit human acceptance.
actual_capabilities: Guide verification through each existing criterion and record PROVEN, FAILED, NOT-RUN, or UNAVAILABLE outcomes.
Record project branch, commit, and worktree state alongside verification results.
Structure append-only outcome rounds with requirement text, commands, observed output, and evidence citations.
Provide a single-criterion evidence runner template with commit checks, refusal conditions, and a five-line report.
Require suitable unit, integration, smoke, manual, or static evidence rather than treating every passing check as equivalent.
Guide output redaction, companion secret scans, failure routing, and human acceptance before completion.
limitations: Companion Executor documentation and helper scripts are referenced but are not included in the two reviewed files.
Requires an existing verification strategy and usable test capabilities; missing prerequisites remain explicit gaps.
Does not fix application failures or independently approve completion; fixes and residual acceptance belong to other participants.
Regression reverts need isolation, and secret-scan recovery needs retained-copy cleanup before evidence is committed.

use_cases.title: Verify a Feature Before Handoff
use_cases.description: Walk existing acceptance criteria, gather suitable evidence, and present unresolved requirements before a feature handoff.

use_cases.title: Review Requirement Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare observed test and smoke outcomes with requirements, without treating a passing unit suite as full feature proof.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Agent Verification
use_cases.description: Dispatch one evidence runner per criterion, inspect the returned artifact, and route failures back to the owning implementation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Requirement
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify criterion [reference] in [verification document] at the current state. Report its requirement, named method, observed output, and status without changing code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: verify a single existing acceptance criterion.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Outcomes Round
prompt_templates.prompt: Walk every criterion in [verification document]. Record state, commands, outcomes, and evidence citations. Summarize all four statuses and stop for human acceptance.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: complete a requirement-level verification ledger.

prompt_templates.title: Dispatch an Evidence Runner
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare one runner for [criterion] using the provided template. Fill every placeholder, select a model explicitly, and verify prerequisites before dispatch.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a bounded single-criterion evidence capture.

prompt_templates.title: Reverify After a Shared-Code Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Review fix [commit] against the existing ledger. Identify affected criteria and append a new round. Use isolated regression checks and scan retained evidence before committing.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: revalidate affected evidence without disturbing shared work.

output: Evidence: none; no run and no evidence file.
Reason: the criterion requires a credential that was not provided.
Do not inspect the environment for secrets or assume the criterion passes.

best_practices: Record the exact tested state and match each requirement to the evidence type its strategy names.
Use an isolated worktree for regression reverts and preserve all existing user changes.
Redact before capture, scan every retained evidence attempt, and resolve sensitive originals before tracking or committing.
anti_patterns: Treating passing unit tests, clean review reports, or expected output as proof of every requirement.
Changing code during verification to obtain a passing result without a separate fix and new evidence round.
Hiding FAILED, NOT-RUN, or UNAVAILABLE outcomes when presenting the completion summary.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It guides checks against existing verification criteria and records observed outcomes. It does not invent acceptance criteria or guarantee software correctness.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists all three tools. The workflow still requires command execution, repository access, and the referenced Executor dependencies.

faq.question: Are the helper scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed skill contains instructions and an evidence runner template. Companion Executor helpers are referenced separately and were not audited here.

faq.question: What happens when a check cannot run?
faq.answer: Record NOT-RUN or UNAVAILABLE with the exact blocker. Missing evidence is not a pass, and residual gaps require explicit human acceptance.

faq.question: Does verification fix failing code?
faq.answer: No. Failures return to execution. After fixes land, append a new round and reverify every criterion the change could affect.

faq.question: What precautions apply to stored evidence?
faq.answer: Redact sensitive output before writing and scan retained files. A redacted replacement does not guarantee earlier sensitive attempts were removed.
